column1: # Buzz corpus replay assessment — curated against the block/buzz commit pinned in
# project.conf. Line ranges index into corpus/<migration>.sql at exactly that pin: bumping
# the pin means re-curating this file (that coupling is deliberate — an assessment must
# never silently apply to a corpus it was not written against).
# One row per replay step, in strict corpus order:
#   execute          run through `pg-sprite migrate`; require exit 0 and outcome
#                    executed-natively — pg-sprite itself mutates the database
#   refuse:<reason>  run through `pg-sprite migrate`; require exit 2 and outcome
#                    refused with exactly <reason> (a reason mismatch is a failure,
#                    not a pass); then apply the same statement via psql to advance
#   psql             out-of-scope content (data changes, PL/pgSQL functions and
#                    triggers, dynamic DO blocks, session-scoped LOCK/SET LOCAL):
#                    applied via psql in one transaction, never assessed
# class (optional, refuse rows only) — what kind of refusal this is, so the
# bucket summary separates missing capability from deliberate scope:
#   (empty)                    capability boundary — pg-sprite is expected to
#   no-online-safety-problem   bootstrap DDL on objects nothing reads yet
#                              is no concurrent-access problem to solve
#   by-design                  refused deliberately and permanently; a safer
#                              form exists (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS — the
#                              name-only no-op cannot prove an existing index
#                              is valid; use plain CREATE INDEX)
# Unnamed ADD FOREIGN KEY: the safer NOT VALID + VALIDATE sequence needs a
# constraint name to reference; the same constraint with CONSTRAINT <name> executes.
# CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS is refused by design: the safer concurrent
# rewrite cannot honor a name-only no-op that proves nothing about whether
# the existing index is valid or even the requested one.
